The instant criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.PC for quashing of FIR No.173/2016 registered at Police Station Virat Nagar, Distt. Jaipur Rural for the offence under Sections 420, 463, 464, 467, 468, 469, 470, 471 & 120B IPC.

entities.text: Police Station Virat Nagar, Distt. Jaipur Rural
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner No.1- Mr. Hem Chand Jat, is present in person before this Court and submits that the all the accused-petitioners [2023/RJJP/003199] (2 of 3) [CRLMP-2092/2018] have amicably settled their dispute with the complainant- respondent and a compromise has been arrived at in between them.
The parties do not wish to continue the criminal proceedings further.

He further submits that in compliance of the directions passed by this Court vide order dated 25.01.2023, the SHO, Police Station Virat Nagar (Jaipur Rural), has submitted his report No.610 dated 13.02.2023 contending therein that there remains no controversy in between both the parties and they have settled their dispute by an amicable settlement and a compromise deed has also been executed in between them.
Learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the miscellaneous petition.

sentences.text: The complainant-respondent- Mr. Ram Karan, is present in person before this Court and submits that both the parties have settled their dispute amicably and he has no objection if the FIR and all other criminal proceedings pending in pursuance thereof against the accused-petitioners, is quashed and set aside.
Heard, perused the material available on record more particularly the Police report, nature of allegation and the compromise deed executed in between the parties.
The parties to the lis have resolved their dispute amicably and do not wish to continue the criminal proceedings and have jointly prayed for quashing of the same.

The offence alleged in this matter is non- compoundable,
however Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
has propounded that if it is convinced that offences are entirely personal in nature and do not affect the public peace or tranquility [2023/RJJP/003199] (3 of 3) [CRLMP-2092/2018] and where it feels that quashing of such proceedings on account of compromise would bring about peace and would secure ends of justice, the High Court should not hesitate to quash the same by exercising the inherent powers vested in it.

entities.text: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Here in this case, both the parties have entered into compromise and the same has also been verified by the SHO concerned.

Though, the parties have settled the dispute amicably and that is essentially in between the parties which is not affecting public peace and tranquility therefore with a view to maintain the harmony and to resolve the dispute finally in between the parties, it is deemed appropriate to quash the entire criminal proceedings undertaken in pursuance thereof.

Accordingly, the criminal misc. Petition is allowed and the FIR No.173/2016 registered at Police Station Virat Nagar, Distt. Jaipur Rural and all further proceedings, are hereby quashed and set aside.
